title: Human Pancreas PACT Optical Clearing and High Resolution 3D Microscopy
author: Elizabeth Butterworth
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9gbh3sn
materials: Incubate the sample with primary antibodies.

Add secondary antibodies at a concentration of 1:200 (5 μl in 1 mL buffer). NOTE: Small format antibodies are preferred, as well as highly cross-adsorbed antibodies if using more than one primary antibody.

steps.title: Tissue Fixation
steps.instruction: Fix the pancreas sample (≤ 1 x 1 x 2 cm) in freshly prepared 4% PFA at 4 °C for 48 h.

substeps.instruction: If the sample is larger than 1 x 1 x 2 cm, dissect into smaller pieces no more than 1 cm thick using a scalpel or razor blade.
Wash the tissue sample in three changes of 0.01 M PBS for at least 15 min each wash.
Store in 15 mL centrifuge tube in 0.01 % PFA/0.01 M PBS or 0.5 % sodium azide/0.01 M PBS until use.

steps.title: Tissue Sectioning
steps.instruction: Section the fixed tissue into 1 - 2 mm thick sections using a vibratome to ensure even sectioning.

steps.title: Paraffin Removal (Deparaffinization)
steps.instruction: Remove paraffin from the tissue sections through a series of solvent washes.

substeps.instruction: Use a new razor blade or scalpel to cut through the paraffin perpendicular to the surface; loosen and remove tissue with forceps or a spatula, gently scraping excess paraffin.
Incubate tissue in xylene (~30 mL for a 3 x 3 x 3 mm section) for 24 h at room temperature (RT).
Transfer to a second container of fresh xylene (same volume) and incubate for 24 h at RT.
Transfer to 100% ethanol (same volume) and incubate for 24 h at RT.
Transfer to 95% ethanol (same volume) and incubate for 24 h at RT.
Transfer to 70% ethanol (same volume) and incubate for 24 h at RT.
Rinse in 0.01 M phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and equilibrate in 0.01 M PBS in a conical tube for 24 h at RT, ensuring tissue is free of paraffin.

steps.title: Prepare A4P1 Hydrogel Monomer Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare 200 mL of 4% acrylamide/1% paraformaldehyde (A4P1) hydrogel monomer solution.

substeps.instruction: Place a flask on ice on a magnetic stir plate with a stir bar.
Add the following in order: 147.8 mL cold (4 - 8 °C) ddH2O, 20 mL 0.1 M PBS, 20 mL cold (4 - 8 °C) 40 % acrylamide solution, 12.2 mL 16 % PFA solution, and 250 mg VA-044 initiator.
Mix with a magnetic stir bar for at least 10 min and keep on ice.

steps.title: Hydrogel Polymerization
steps.instruction: Embed the tissue sections in the A4P1 hydrogel and polymerize.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 14 mL of monomer solution into a 15-mL conical tube on ice and add one 1-2 mm thick tissue sample; cap the tube.
Remove oxygen from the solution by bubbling gaseous N2 through the liquid for 10 min using 18-gauge hypodermic needles (one submerged for input, one for venting).
Quickly remove needles and seal the cap with paraffin film to prevent gas exchange.
Incubate the degassed sample at 37 °C for 3 h to polymerize the hydrogel.

steps.title: Post-Polymerization Wash
steps.instruction: Remove excess hydrogel and wash the samples.

substeps.instruction: Pour away excess hydrogel into a chemical waste container and gently wipe the sample with a paper towel.
Wash on a shaker at 60 rpm at RT for one day with 40 mL 0.01 M PBS, changing the buffer 4-5 times (every hour until the final wash).
Allow the final wash to continue overnight at RT.

steps.title: Tissue Clearing
steps.instruction: Clear the hydrogel-embedded tissue using SDS buffer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 500 mL clearing solution (4% SDS, pH 8.5): add 50 mL 0.1 M PBS and 20 g SDS powder to ~300 mL ddH2O; adjust to pH 8.5 using NaOH and HCl, then bring to 500 mL with ddH2O.
Wash the sample in 3-5 exchanges of 0.01 M PBS for 15 min each.
Transfer the sample to a 50-mL conical tube with 40 mL of clearing buffer.
Incubate at 37 °C, changing to fresh clearing buffer every other day.
Continue clearing for 2-8 weeks (e.g., ~8 weeks for a 3 mm x 3 mm x 3 mm sample) until the sample is adequately transparent.

steps.title: Primary Antibody Staining
steps.instruction: Perform immunohistochemistry on the cleared tissue.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PACT staining buffer: add 50 mg sodium azide and 0.5 mL TritonX-100 to 500 mL 0.01 M PBS.

Prepare primary antibody solution: add 2% normal serum (same species as secondary antibody) and primary antibody (use ~5x the concentration of standard IHC, e.g., 1:100 instead of 1:500) to the PACT staining buffer in a 2-mL flat-bottom tube (min 1 mL total volume).
Remove sample from wash buffer, dab excess off with a paper towel, and place in the primary antibody solution.
Incubate for 2-4 days at RT on a shaker at 60 rpm.
Wash samples at RT on a shaker at 60 rpm in 0.01 M PBS, changing buffer 4-5 times and leaving the final wash overnight.

steps.title: Secondary Antibody Staining
steps.instruction: Apply secondary antibodies to the sample.

substeps.instruction: Prepare secondary antibody solution: add 2% normal serum (same species as secondary antibody) and secondary antibody to PACT staining buffer in a 2-mL flat-bottom tube (1 mL total volume).
Remove sample from wash buffer, dab excess off, and place in the secondary antibody solution.
Incubate at RT on a shaker at 60 rpm for 2 days, protected from light.
Wash samples at RT on a shaker at 60 rpm in 0.01 M PBS, changing buffer 4-5 times and leaving the final wash overnight, protected from light.

steps.title: Refractive Index Matching (RIMS)
steps.instruction: Equilibrate the sample in Refractive Index Matched Solution (RIMS).

substeps.instruction: Prepare RIMS: weigh 11 g non-ionic density gradient medium (e.g., Histodenz) into a 50-mL conical tube; add ~5 mL 0.02 M phosphate buffer (PB), mix well to release air, and bring final volume to 10 mL with PB.
Incubate RIMS at 37 °C until dissolved, inverting and mixing as needed.
Pipette 1 mL RIMS into a 2-mL flat-bottom tube; remove sample from wash buffer, dab excess off, and place in RIMS.
Gently tap the tube to submerge the sample; incubate on the bench at RT, protected from light, for 2-4 days.
Ensure the sample has equilibrated in RIMS for at least 24 h before imaging.

steps.title: Sample Mounting and Imaging
steps.instruction: Mount the sample and acquire 3D images using a lightsheet microscope.

substeps.instruction: Place a small amount of RIMS into an 8-well coverslip bottom chamber slide (just enough to coat the bottom) and add the sample; cap the slide.
Alternatively, for lightsheet microscopy, use a small (black) capillary; glue the tissue to the end of the capillary using super glue, touching as little surface as possible.
Image using 5X or 25X objectives with the pivot scan option.
Set up acquisition: use a z-step smaller than optimal (e.g., 1 μm) if deconvolution is desired.
Begin nearest the tissue surface, increasing gain as the objective focuses through the z-plane (do not change laser settings).
Acquire a test stack (1 average, 512 x 512 resolution, max speed) to check for equal brightness across colors in 3D.
Acquire final high-resolution z-stack: max speed, 16 bit, 4 or more averages, 1024 x 1024 resolution or better, zooming into the object to reduce photo-bleaching.
